<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A new `"example-tree"` stage will be inserted after `"data"` to display the example tree with boundaries.

The stage will animate tree growth and synchronize scatter plot boundaries with revealNodes. Changes span types.ts, stages.ts, tutorial.ts, and ForestDemo.tsx.

The example-tree stage will reuse the existing grow animation. It will hide the tree picker and focus on tree zero. Unlike the grow stage, it will also render boundaries on the scatter plot.

The new step precedes train-yourself. It serves as a passive demo where students first see how a tree draws boundaries and grows. The grow stage remains after train-yourself and may overlap slightly.

The example-tree stage will use `forest.trees[0]` and animate `revealNodes` from 1 to total nodes. It will render splits and leaf regions on the scatter plot, optionally highlighting the active split. A ref-based trigger will drive the growth animation, following the same pattern used by the grow stage.

The existing grow animation effect resets its trigger ref whenever the stage changes. This would prevent the example-tree stage from starting its own growth animation. The effect will be updated to also trigger on example-tree, or a separate ref will be used.

The grow animation effect will be extended to trigger on both the grow and example-tree stages. TreeView will receive revealNodes during example-tree while hiding them during the grow stage. The scatter plot will compute revealed splits from the first tree using the current revealNodes count.

The example-tree stage will pass computed splits, leaf regions, and the active split ID to the scatter plot. Left and right split highlighting will be included for consistency with the training overlay, though this may be overkill for a tutorial. Bag indices or full data will be needed to support that highlighting.

The example tree will use all data points rather than just the bootstrap bag. This lets students see how the tree partitions the full dataset. Split left and right regions will be highlighted for all samples inside each active split. The tutorial text will describe the computer splitting space with lines that ask questions about width or length.

The tutorial title will be "How one tree learns" or "Drawing boundaries." The scatter plot will color regions to show where the tree would guess each species. Step numbering in stages.ts will shift: train-yourself becomes step 3 and grow becomes step 4.
